### Problem description

We are reproducing OpenVLA-OFT reinforcement learning (GRPO) on RoboTwin. Only the “total_num_envs: 128 -> 32” and "group_size: 8 -> 4" in the default config. With this change, the rollout phase is very slow（30:15 for 1 training step, 8 rollout_epochs）. We suspect that parallel robotwin environment execution on 8*H200 is not scaling well in my conda environment, so rollout becomes the bottleneck. We are looking for the intended way to speed up so that rollout time stays acceptable.

[config.yaml](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25186342/config.yaml)

## Potential Causes and Solutions

### 1. **Environment Parallelization Configuration**

The RLinf project uses a distributed rollout system. Make sure your configuration properly enables GPU-parallelized environments:

```yaml
# Check these settings in your config
rollout:
  num_envs_per_gpu: 4  # Adjust based on your GPU memory
  env_type: "robotwin"  # Ensure this is set correctly
```

### 2. **CUDA Graphs**

Recent versions of RLinf support CUDA graphs for faster rollout. Check if this is enabled:

```yaml
actor:
  use_cuda_graph: true  # Can significantly speed up inference
```

hi @DS-Zeng , RLinf supports specifying the number of envs per gpu. It is `total_num_envs` divided by the number of GPUs you allocated to env worker group (e.g., `component_placement`).

It is a complex task to tune the training of embodied and RL, as the characteristics of different simulators are very different. RLinf supports flexible configuration of the GPUs allocated to env/rollout/training. But users still need to profile the components (i.e., workers) of the RL process to decide a more efficient `component_placement` configuration. We are also working on developing an automatic configuration tool, will release it in the future.

It has come to our attention that some common techniques could improve current throughput and further imporve overall efficiency under robotwin settings. By setting` env.train.task_config.clear_cache_freq: 8` could reduce single time env bootstrap reset time from ~400s to ~70s depending on the specific test case you use. And env bootstrap is typically on the critical path.  Another approach is setting pipeline_stage to 2, this allows rollout and env worker sharing the same gpu at the same time, when SMs are not fully utilized this will lead to a overall improvement in rollout generation phase. However, in robotwin scenarios, this probably provide limited improvement as env cost is way larger than rollout worker.
